newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco, Merrill settle copper futures dispute.
newsitem.headline: Codelco, Merrill settle copper futures dispute.

text.p: Merrill Lynch and Co. Inc. agreed Tuesday to pay Chilean state copper giant Codelco $25 million to settle a dispute resulting from a copper futures trading scandal that shook world metals markets in 1994.
The settlement is related to trading done by a former Codelco trader, Juan Pablo Davila, that cost the corporation about $170 million.
Codelco had accused Merrill, which was Codelco's leading broker, of allowing Davila to make unauthorised trades.

Merrill denied any complicity in Davila's trading and a statement released by the two companies said an investigation by Codelco failed to find evidence of illicit payments by Merrill Lynch to Davila.

"Although Merrill Lynch denies having done anything incorrect, it will pay Codelco $25 million to put an end to this dispute and avoid the costs that are involved in continuing," said Codelco President Marcos Lima, who read the statement.
Merrill's payment will include $22 million to cover Codelco's losses and $3 million toward its legal costs.
The settlement is the first Codelco has made following a three-year probe into Davila's deals, which forced the resignation in disgrace of its then president.
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, has started court cases in London against Belgian and German brokers, accusing them of paying secret commissions to Davila.
Davila, who was fired when the losses were uncovered in 1994, has been charged with fraud and carrying out business "incompatible" with his position in Codelco.
